hero.title: Machines cross borders.
hero.intro: AI agents already act across clouds, organizations, and jurisdictions. But when one sovereign system encounters another, there is no neutral protocol for answering three basic questions:
questions: What are you allowed to do?
hero.statement: Genesis Mesh is a treaty layer for machines.
hero.body: Independent authorities can recognize identities, delegate capabilities, and revoke trust across organizational and national boundaries, without surrendering their own root of trust.
hero.notLine: No central authority. No shared sovereign. No required cloud.
hero.closing: Trust that no nation has to surrender.

trustCycle.label: One Complete Trust Cycle
trustCycle.title: The same request changes when trust changes.
trustCycle.subtitle: Two independently governed systems establish scoped recognition, make an authorization decision, propagate revocation, and produce an auditable rejection without sharing a root of trust.
trustCycle.sameRequest: Same identity. Same request. Different trust state.

steps.title: Attestation issued
steps.description: Sovereign B signs an attestation for the requesting identity.

steps.title: Treaty recognized
steps.description: Sovereign A activates a scoped recognition treaty for Sovereign B.

steps.title: Request accepted
steps.description: The attestation and treaty satisfy A's local authorization policy.

steps.title: Attestation revoked
steps.description: Sovereign B withdraws that specific trust material.

steps.title: Revocation imported
steps.description: A verifies B's signed feed and updates its own trust state.

steps.title: Identical request rejected
steps.description: The same identity and request now fail with an auditable reason.

stakes.label: Sovereignty
stakes.title: Sovereignty without isolation.
stakes.subtitle: Independent systems need to cooperate without requiring political alignment, shared infrastructure, or a common root of trust.
stakes.notLine: Genesis Mesh handles the machine-legible subset of that relationship: recognition, scope, delegation, revocation, and evidence.
stakes.boundary: It does not negotiate policy, arbitrate disputes, or govern participants. Those remain human and institutional responsibilities.

powers.label: Cooperation
powers.title: Cooperation does not require alignment.
powers.subtitle: Genesis Mesh does not encode alliances. The protocol requires cryptographic recognition, not political agreement.

close.title: Shared work, separate authority.
close.desc: Authorities can cooperate closely while each retains its own keys, policy, and revocation power.

scoped.title: One transaction can be enough.
scoped.desc: Recognition may cover one role, one purpose, or one time window without creating a permanent alliance.

different.title: Recognition is not endorsement.
different.desc: Authorities with different policies can verify a bounded relationship without claiming broader political agreement.
examples: Either authority can revoke its own trust

mechanics.label: The Mechanics
mechanics.title: Infrastructure that encodes no politics - only mechanics.
mechanics.subtitle: Most trust infrastructure encodes the politics of whoever runs the root. Genesis Mesh encodes only four operations and leaves the politics to the sovereigns. That is what makes it treaty-grade rather than vendor-grade.

ops.name: Verify
ops.desc: Cryptographic proof of who holds authority - Ed25519 identity, signed genesis blocks, evidence chains.

ops.name: Limit
ops.desc: Scoped, time-bounded delegations. Capability manifests define what each identity may do - nothing more.

ops.name: Revoke
ops.desc: The moment trust breaks, signed revocation propagates across sovereign boundaries - and is honored.

ops.name: Audit
ops.desc: Every decision leaves tamper-evident evidence. No one has to take your word for it.

evidence.title: Why not SPIFFE, DID, or OAuth?

protocol.label: The Protocol
protocol.title: An open RFC program - standards-shaped, not vendor-shaped.
protocol.subtitle: The Python reference implementation and TypeScript, Go, and .NET SDKs are coordinated at v0.56.0. The core suite has 1,327 tests, with formal protocol evidence documented for Tamarin verification.

l1.name: Protocol Core
l1.desc: Ed25519 identity, signed genesis blocks, enrollment, revocation, routing, audit.

l2.name: Sovereign Communities
l2.desc: Independent trust domains. Each controls its own membership, governance, revocation.

l3.name: Recognition Network
l3.desc: Treaties between sovereigns. Trust paths and revocation propagation across boundaries.

governance.label: Protocol Governance
governance.title: Open change, explicit authority.
governance.description: Protocol changes move through public drafts, maintainer review, operator review when obligations change, security review for trust-state changes, and dated decisions.
governance.boundary: The reference implementation is not the protocol. Operators retain their own keys, policies, trust decisions, and exit rights.

live.title: Maintainer-Operated Public Deployment
live.subtitle: Independent Keys / Independent Policy / Reproducible Proofs

silicon.label: Research
silicon.title: Sovereign Compute
silicon.subtitle: TSWI explores the hardware layer beneath software sovereignty: operator-owned packaging, interposer design, orchestration, and energy-aware compute infrastructure.
silicon.conclusion: This is a separate research track, not a requirement for adopting the Genesis Mesh protocol.

live.label: Live
live.title: Not a promise. A running system.
live.subtitle: Maintainer-operated public deployment with independently reproducible protocol proofs.

closing.title: Build with Genesis Mesh.
closing.subtitle: Choose the adoption path that matches your role without surrendering your own trust decisions.

builders.title: Spin up your own sovereign trust domain.
builders.desc: Read the RFCs, pull the TypeScript / Go / .NET SDKs, and stand up an L2 Sovereign Community on infrastructure you already own.

strategic.title: Evaluate the protocol, proof, and governance boundary.
strategic.desc: Review the public architecture and reproducible evidence, then open a direct channel for institutional deployment questions.

seo.description: A sovereign trust, identity & communication fabric for autonomous systems. Sovereignty-neutral, treaty-grade: verify, limit, revoke, audit. Not a blockchain. Not a VPN. Not a service mesh.
